hypothesis: Small-cap sector-bucketed pairs trading: relative-value mean-reversion between cointegrated, same-industry pairs, entered on 2-sigma spread divergence, exited on 0.5-sigma reversion or forced close. Genuinely new mechanism (relative-value between pairs), distinct from every prior cross-sectional single-factor trial in this registry. Multiple-testing control via sector bucketing + hierarchical clustering + BH-FDR-corrected Engle-Granger cointegration + a 2-consecutive-formation-period persistence filter (the direct analog of this registry's DSR discipline, applied to pair selection instead of trial selection).

notes: STOP -- zero trades under the pre-registered methodology; no return series, Sharpe/CALMAR/beta/DSR not computable. NOT relaxed/re-tuned after seeing this (that would defeat the trial's own multiple-testing discipline). DIAGNOSTIC SUPPLEMENT ONLY (NOT this trial's registered result, NOT itself additionally FDR-corrected for the multiple-testing the persistence filter exists to control): bypassing the persistence filter and trading the 9 raw per-cycle FDR-survivor pairs directly gives 16 trades (win rate 43.8% overall -- 62.5% for converged exits avg 28d, only 25.0% for forced-close exits avg 100d). Net monthly (61mo): ann_ret=-4.44% Sharpe=-0.454 CALMAR=-0.183 MaxDD=-24.21% t=-1.02. Gross monthly: ann_ret=-0.54% Sharpe=-0.017 MaxDD=-17.96% -- gross is near-breakeven-to-negative, not a clear 'good signal ruined by cost' story; cost drag ~404bps/yr deepens an already-weak gross result. Realized beta vs IWM = -0.097 (t=-1.81, not significant) -- the low-beta motivating premise is roughly validated (not significantly different from zero) even in this small, non-registered sample. Only 329/1306 business days (25%) had any capital deployed at all across the 5-year window.
trial_note: New independent trial, new mechanism family. Pre-registered methodology (sector bucket -> hierarchical clustering, distance threshold 0.4/corr>=0.6, cluster size 2-8 -> Engle-Granger cointegration, BH-FDR alpha=0.05 pooled per formation cycle across all buckets -> 2-consecutive-cycle persistence filter) run exactly as specified, NOT relaxed after seeing results. Result: ZERO pairs ever achieved 2-consecutive-cycle persistence across all 10 rolling cycles (2015-2021) -- STOP disposition, not a Sharpe/DSR failure (no return series exists to evaluate). Verified not a bug: cycle 8's 5 FDR survivors (CCS-LGIH, CCS-MTH, CCS-TMHC, LGIH-TMHC, AEIS-ICHR -- all economically sensible same-industry pairs, homebuilders + semiconductor-equipment) share zero overlap with cycle 9's 2 survivors (RTX-VC, BBSI-HRI) -- confirmed by direct inspection of per-cycle survivor sets. Key structural finding: same-sector pairwise correlations in this $100M-2B universe are much lower than large-cap pairs-trading intuition (bucket mean correlation ~0.2-0.3, max rarely above 0.6), which is why hierarchical clustering narrows 59,687 within-bucket candidate pairs down to just 307 -- small/mid caps are structurally more idiosyncratic than the mechanism's implicit large-cap-pairs-trading prior assumes. adjClose used for BOTH signal AND P&L throughout (not the registry's usual adjClose-signal/raw-close-return split) because in pairs trading signal and return are the same price series -- a raw-close split/dividend artifact in either leg would corrupt the cointegration test, generate spurious entries/exits, AND misstate P&L simultaneously. Formation/trading leakage audit: PASS by construction (trading_start == formation_end exactly every cycle; hedge ratio and spread mean/std frozen at formation end, never recomputed mid-trading).

hypothesis: George & Hwang (2004) 52-week-high anchoring: investors anchor on a stock's 52-week high as a psychological ceiling; stocks trading NEAR their 52-week high see good news underreacted to, producing positive drift. Long top quintile nearness (adjClose / trailing 252-day high), short bottom quintile. Genuinely distinct mechanism from S1/S4 (IVOL/MAX) -- anchoring to a slow-moving reference price, not extreme recent-return behavior.
data_source: Tiingo (adjClose for signal, raw close for returns) + SEC shares-outstanding facts only (already cached from S9/S1/S4, no new fetches, no GP/A-style financial-statement dependency)
notes: FAILS DSR (per_period_sr=-0.2621 < threshold=0.2063, N=25). MOMENTUM INDEPENDENCE CHECK (the core secondary test): mean cross-sectional Spearman correlation between nearness and 12-1 momentum = 0.611 (range 0.415 to 0.798, 82% of periods >0.5) -- CONTRADICTS the original literature's 'largely independent' claim in this small/mid-cap universe; the two signals are meaningfully correlated. Fama-MacBeth (return ~ nearness_rank + momentum_rank, both included jointly): mean b_nearness=-0.0198 (t=-1.644) -- WRONG-SIGNED and only marginally significant once momentum is controlled for; mean b_momentum=0.0134 (t=1.882) -- correctly signed, also marginal. CONCLUSION: nearness-to-52-week-high does NOT look like a genuinely distinct, exploitable mechanism in this universe -- univariate IC is already ~null (t=0.24), the signal is highly correlated with momentum (contradicting the paper's independence premise), and controlling for momentum flips its sign rather than confirming independent predictive power. It reads as a weaker, noisier restatement of momentum here, not a new mechanism. 2020 SUB-PERIOD: catastrophic (-59.4% for the year alone; 4 of 12 months had |return|>15%), with the worst months (April +26.8% mkt, November +22.3% mkt) occurring DURING market recovery rallies -- consistent with a momentum-crash-style regime sensitivity (long near-high/recent-winners, short far-below/recent-losers gets destroyed when the most beaten-down names rally hardest). Global max drawdown (-75.7%) spans peak 2016-01 to trough 2020-11 -- a 4+ year continuous underwater period, not a single-year event. High cost drag (~1305 bps/yr) from monthly rebalance turnover (~35%/month) further compounds an already-negative gross result (-8.37%/yr) -- not a 'good signal ruined by costs' story either.

notes: Side observation (partial, order-biased sample -- the 233 tickers whose CUSIPs resolved before the quota wall hit, NOT a clean random sample of the universe, reported for context only, not as a validated coverage statistic): of 142 resolved 2015 $100M-2B universe names, 116 (81.7%) were held by >=1 13F filer as of 2015-01-01 (filing-date gated, using 2014q4+2015q1 bulk SEC data); of 180 resolved 2020 universe names, 159 (88.3%) were held by >=1 13F filer as of 2020-01-01 (using 2019q4+2020q1 bulk SEC data). This suggests institutional 13F coverage in this universe is likely HIGH if the crosswalk problem were solved -- a promising signal for a future attempt, not a reason this trial's Phase 1 stop is itself in question. VERDICT: kill before backtest. To resume: either (a) wait for the FMP quota to reset (unconfirmed reset period, likely daily for this tier) and spread the ~3,300-ticker crosswalk across multiple sessions/days, or (b) source CUSIPs from a different vendor/tier -- a real budget/time decision left to the user, not assumed. Not fixed here.

hypothesis: Cluster-conditioned short-term mean reversion: within sector-bucketed, loosely-correlated clusters (realized avg intra-cluster corr ~0.2, deliberately weaker than S18's pairwise cointegration bar), a member deviating >2.5 sigma from the cluster's leave-one-out equal-weighted average (formation-period-normalized) is traded long/short against the cluster basket, exiting on reversion to |z|<0.5 or a 5-day forced close. Hybrid mechanism: basket-relative (not S18's strict pairwise cointegration) short-term reversal (not S8's full-cross-section ranking), testing whether cluster-conditioning fixes either S18's near-zero-candidate problem or S8's high-IC-but-gross-negative problem.

notes: PRIMARY (basket) construction: Sharpe(net,ann)=-17.4111 CALMAR=-0.6675 ann_net=-66.4431% ann_gross=5.7764% maxDD(net)=-99.5338% beta_vs_IWM=+0.0900 (t=+2.817) cost_drag=10999bps/yr n_months=60. HEADLINE FINDING: this is a REAL, POSITIVE gross signal (gross Sharpe=0.954, gross CALMAR=0.653, gross ann_ret=5.78%, gross win_rate=55%, IC(|entry_z| vs trade_gross, per-cycle)=+0.0207 t=+1.566, n_cycles=10/10 -- positive and borderline-significant, bigger dislocations DO modestly predict bigger reversion gains) -- COMPLETELY DESTROYED by transaction costs at this trading frequency: net Sharpe=-17.41, net ann_ret=-66.4%, cost_drag~11000bps/yr (~110%/yr). This is the cleanest and MOST EXTREME version of the S2/S8 'high-quality-signal-killed-by-cost' pattern in this registry -- unlike S8 (gross itself negative, -3.08%/yr) or S2 (gross -4.74%/yr), S21's gross Sharpe of 0.95 would clear the promotion bar on its own; the entire failure is attributable to trading frequency (avg 4.9-day holds, 4683 round trips over 60 months, ~2.67% round-trip cost each) rather than signal quality. Only 0.36% of trades exit via genuine Z-score convergence (|z|<0.5 within 5 days); 99.6% are force-closed on the 5-day timer -- the reversion mechanism almost never completes within the pre-registered window, but still generates enough net positive drift on average (mean trade_gross=0.1900%, aggregated across 4,683 quasi-independent bets via breadth) to produce a respectable GROSS Sharpe -- a textbook small-edge/high-breadth effect that transaction costs (charged per round trip, not amortized by breadth) completely negate. Concentration: top sector = 16.8% of total |trade PnL| mass across 19 sectors with trades -- clean, no single sector dominating. Selectivity funnel (10 cycles, GGR rolling): avg universe 414 names/cycle -> 3085 bucketed (sum) -> 637 raw clusters at CLUSTER_DIST_THRESH=0.8 -> 109 in the pre-registered [4,15] size range -> 109 tradeable clusters (848 member-slots) -> 4683 entries -> 4683 trades closed. REALIZED avg intra-cluster correlation = 0.328 (median 0.306) -- directly comparable to S18's own diagnosed same-sector bucket-mean of 0.2-0.3: this trial's clusters landed almost exactly on that 'typical' level (as intended by the deliberately more permissive 0.8 distance cut vs S18's 0.4/>=0.6 cut) -- CONFIRMS clusters here really are the 'weaker, basket-level' relationship the trial set out to test, not accidentally another high-correlation subset. SECONDARY (peer) construction: Sharpe(net)=-9.3946 Sharpe(gross)=0.6230 CALMAR(net)=-0.6263 ann_net=-62.1088% beta=+0.0742 (t=+1.340) IC=+0.0393 (t=+1.605) -- same pattern (real positive gross edge, cost-destroyed net), somewhat weaker gross Sharpe than basket; basket-vs-single-nearest-peer referencing is not the deciding factor for this trial's outcome, cost frequency is. VERDICT ON THE TWO MOTIVATING QUESTIONS: (1) vs S18's pairwise-correlation problem: cluster-average referencing DID successfully produce a large, non-zero trade count (basket: 4683 trades, peer: 4858 trades, vs S18's 0 trades) at a realized correlation level (~0.33) where S18's stricter pairwise cointegration+FDR+persistence discipline produced nothing -- the basket-relative mechanism is unambiguously more tradeable in the sense of generating both a testable sample size AND a real positive gross IC/Sharpe, which S18 never even got to test. (2) vs S8's gross-negative problem: cluster-conditioning DID fix it, decisively -- gross Sharpe went from S8's implicit negative-gross regime to a genuinely attractive 0.95 here. But fixing that problem surfaced an even MORE severe one: the 5-day-hold/2.5-sigma-entry construction trades so frequently (avg 4.9-day hold vs GP/S7/S8's quarterly-to-monthly cadence) that realistic transaction costs overwhelm even a genuinely good gross signal by an order of magnitude -- this trial's own pre-registered 'HIGH cost-drag risk a priori' caution was directionally right but the realized magnitude (~110%/yr cost drag) is far more extreme than anything else in this registry (S2's next-worst cost drag was ~4079bps/yr, i.e. ~2.7x smaller). FAILS DSR at N=27 (per-period SR=-5.0262 vs threshold 0.2306). Promotion criteria (CALMAR>=1 or Sharpe>=0.8) on NET returns NOT MET (gross alone would have cleared it: gross Sharpe=0.95, gross CALMAR=0.65).
